children: U.S. existing home sales fell 2.0% M/M to 3.98M in August vs. 3.97M consensus and 4.06M recorded in the prior month,
released by the National Association of Realtors on Thursday.
Sales held steady in the West, and declined in the Northeast, Midwest, and South.
Year-over-year, sales dropped 1.2%. Sales were unchanged in the South, and declined in the Northeast, Midwest, and West.
"Mortgage rates and home sales move in opposite directions, so it's not surprising to see a mild dip in home-buying activity due to high mortgage rates," said NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun.
"Still, home prices are rising, and existing home sales are actually up 1.6% year-to-date through the first eight months of the year," said Yun.

"Homebuying demand, despite higher interest rates, is no doubt being supported by rising wages, which grew 3.1% in August, along with 643,000 net new jobs added since the start of the year. Job creation and wage growth typically drive housing demand."

title: Existing home sales fall slightly less than expected in August
